_comment: EXECUTION POLICY — the four things a task needs that the catalogue does not
already say.
WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT HERE. No task definitions. A workflow-template
stage in workflows.json already carries an objective, inputs, actions,
tools, an output, a validation sentence, an owning role, a duration and the
stage that follows it — which is a task template in everything but name.
Writing a second copy of those under a new heading would be the exact
duplication Phase 1 spent a week removing. src/operations/task-template.js
DERIVES the template from the catalogue; this file adds only what the
catalogue has never had a reason to hold.
Four things:
capabilities   the vocabulary an agent is matched against. Roles are who
does the work; capabilities are what the work needs. A
role maps to capabilities, so a stage owned by a designer
requires design capabilities without anyone typing them
onto four hundred stages.
executors      who may execute a stage, derived from the feature's own
automationPotential. `none` means a person, always.
qa             how a quality check is judged: by a machine, by a person,
or both. Defaults, overridable per feature.
limits         retry, timeout and escalation. An agent that never stops
is worse than one that never starts.
_roleCapabilities: WHAT EACH ROLE CAN DO. A stage owned by role.designer requires the
capabilities listed here, so agent matching is structured rather than a
guess at what 'Produce genuinely distinct options.' might need.
role.client is absent on purpose: the client is not matched to anything.
_executors: WHO MAY EXECUTE, read off the feature's own automationPotential rather
than decided again here. `assist` means an agent may draft and a person
finishes — so the task is agent-eligible but its output always goes to a
person. `none` means no agent, ever, whatever an automation rule wants.

none.note: A person. Nothing about this is a machine's to do.

assist.note: An agent may draft it; a person finishes and signs it.

partial.note: An agent may do most of it; a person checks the result.

full.note: An agent may complete it. QA still applies.

_qa: HOW A QUALITY CHECK IS JUDGED. The catalogue writes checks as sentences a
person can act on — 'Text contrast measured, not eyeballed' — which is the
right way to write them and the wrong way to evaluate them by machine. So
every check defaults to a human judgement, and a check becomes automatic
only where something can actually run it. Claiming otherwise would be a QA
_limits: An agent that never stops is worse than one that never starts.
These are the defaults; a task template may lower them, never raise them.
